# Session Plan v2.4

*For: the CEO and the Head of Product. Changes from v2.3: Session 2 moved a week later at your
request; the decision list is now two items.*

## Introduction

You asked for one list, one owner, and a weekly cut. This plan gets there in three sessions. The
first cuts the backlog. The second turns what survives into the queue and names its owner. The
third checks whether the owner is actually cutting.

Throughout, "the queue" means the single ranked list that replaces the backlog after session one.
Nothing enters the queue without an owner's say, and the queue is the only list planning reads from.

## Session 1

Read the top forty backlog items aloud. For each, ask who would object if it were deleted. Delete
the ones with no objector. What survives is the raw material for the queue.

## Session 2

Rank the survivors into the queue. Name the queue's owner. Agree the weekly cut: thirty minutes,
owner reads the queue, cuts what has gone stale, and the team can appeal once per item.

## Session 3

Four weeks after session two, read the queue again. If it is shorter than it was, the cut is
working. If it is longer, the owner is not cutting, and we talk about why rather than about tooling.

## Decisions to Discuss

Two decisions are yours and cannot be delegated. Where the code lives is the CEO's call, because
it sets who can see the queue. Where the queue lives is the Head of Product's call, because it
sets who can edit it. Both need to land before session two, or the queue drifts back into a
backlog. As you put it in the kickoff, ship the boring version first; a shared document beats a
tool nobody has chosen yet.
